chunks: From him, from al-Qasim, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who testified in the testimony of another. He said, 'I did not appoint him as witness,' then he said, 'The testimony of the more just of the two is accepted.'

key_terms.أَعْدَلِهِمَا: The more just of the two

ai.seo_question: How is the validity of a witness determined when one testifies based on another's testimony in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the principle of *ta'dil* (comparative justice) in cases of *shahadat al-shahid* (testimony of testimony) where the original witness was not formally commissioned by the judge. The ruling prioritizes the 'more just' (*a'dal*) of the two witnesses, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on moral integrity (*'adalah*) as the primary criterion for evidentiary validity. This principle ensures judicial fairness by allowing the court to weigh the reliability of indirect testimony based on the comparative piety and trustworthiness of the individuals involved.
